subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate with no noble house affiliation, no known lineage, and no apparent strategic value in Menzoberranzan, yet someone has paid a significant sum — described as 'they interrupt you, a lot' — to ensure his survival.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a Drow mercenary from House Duskryn, hired to protect Daz from House Mizzrym and House T'sarran, who speaks with the practiced tone of Menzoberranzan’s elite, displays professional detachment, and dismisses theological threats as irrelevant to her contract.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a Drow mercenary from House Duskryn, co-hired with Nym to protect Daz; she is analytically sharp, visibly puzzled by the anomaly of Daz’s value, and uninterested in self-mythologizing narratives, yet acknowledges the financial weight behind his protection.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery... Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a Lolth cleric who declared herself in charge after a chaotic escape, displaying unwavering confidence and divine self-justification, ultimately killed by Zalthir to prevent her from invoking further divine power.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-trained individual with an Eldritch Claw Tattoo, who decisively killed Asha Vandree to neutralize a clerical threat, acting when others hesitated, and accepting the moral weight of the choice without justification.
source_quote: I'm making a call." ... "I didn't look at the body.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the party who attempted to subdue Asha Vandree via grapple, believing non-lethal restraint sufficient, but was corrected by the Drow mercenaries for misunderstanding the lethal nature of Lolth clerics.
source_quote: I could have taken her out if I wanted to." ... "I don't like killing people if I don't have to.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a divine caster who attempted to use holy light against Asha Vandree, failed, and later expressed reluctance to kill, preferring alternatives — reflecting his theological ethics and discomfort with lethal force.
source_quote: Let's put a period after that 'now that I'm in charge' thing.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is one of the two noble Drow houses explicitly named as threats to Daz’s life, contracted to be neutralized by the Duskryn sisters as part of their protection contract.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is one of the two noble Drow houses named as threats to Daz’s life, contracted to be neutralized by the Duskryn sisters, who were prepared to handle them personally if necessary.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: House Ilvara
fact: House Ilvara is mentioned as a threat to Daz, though not directly targeted by the Duskryn sisters' contract — implied to be part of the broader network of enemies seeking his death.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: House Duskryn
fact: House Duskryn is the mercenary house to which Nym and Kaelira belong; they operate with professional detachment, contractual precision, and deep familiarity with Menzoberranzan’s power structures, yet remain anonymous agents with no knowledge of their employer.
source_quote: We hoped that you'd be smart enough to avoid Ilvara... well, we could have handled House T'sarran and whatever goons they threw at you.

subject: contract fulfillment
fact: The Duskryn sisters fulfilled their contract to protect Daz from House Mizzrym and House T'sarran, successfully preventing his death during the confrontation, and departed immediately after, indicating their work was complete and payment secured.
source_quote: The contract was fulfilled; they were done.

subject: Asha's execution
fact: Asha Vandree, a Lolth cleric who seized authority after the escape, was executed by Zalthir using his Eldritch Claw Tattoo to prevent her from invoking divine power, ending a potential internal threat to the party’s cohesion.
source_quote: The strikes came in sequence... Asha Vandree did not get another word out.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the Drow city-state where the contract for Daz’s protection originated, a place where noble houses wield lethal political power, financial transactions are heavily insulated, and anonymity implies high stakes or illegality.
source_quote: Someone in Menzoberranzan had spent generously... That level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: the extraction contract
fact: The extraction contract is a document produced by the party that was central to the conflict, apparently detailing the terms of an operation that led to the confrontation with House Mizzrym and House T'sarran, now scorched and referenced as evidence.
source_quote: Kaelira gestured toward the scorched remnants of the extraction contract the party had produced — the document that had apparently been at the center of all this.

subject: T'sarran goons
fact: T'sarran goons are unnamed enforcers or mercenaries loyal to House T'sarran, previously engaged and burned by the party, indicating prior violent conflict and establishing their role as immediate threats.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Daz's hidden identity
fact: A persistent thread surrounds Daz’s origin: why would an unknown, houseless Drow attract such expensive, anonymous protection in Menzoberranzan? The answer remains concealed, suggesting a hidden lineage, a prophecy, or a political game beyond the party’s knowledge.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?

subject: the unknown employer
fact: The identity of the individual or faction who paid for Daz’s protection remains unknown — the contract was mediated through cutouts, and even the Duskryn sisters do not know their employer, implying a conspiracy of significant scale and secrecy.
source_quote: Someone had paid for this. Someone who knew I was here, knew who was hunting me, and knew enough to contract professionals rather than handle it directly.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a session in which the party confronts internal and external threats following an escape from a hostile extraction, leading to moral decisions and revelations about Daz’s value.
source_quote: The sisters departed. Professionally. Without ceremony.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is a halfling author whose writings Daz has read extensively; his phrase 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything' resonates with Daz’s current existential realization.
source_quote: He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who became indistinguishable from Zuggtmoy’s rot, and was looted with efficient respect after her theological problem was resolved.
source_quote: So I looted her with the efficient respect one extends to a theological problem that has been resolved.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth subverted by Zuggtmoy, whose prayer book documented a slow, ambiguous corruption through marginalia in a second handwriting.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Two hands because two minds had been working the same pen.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had his tooth collected as a trophy by Ilvara, and reclaimed it from her confiscated belongings after recognizing its significance.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back. He held it for a moment without saying anything.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym sent frantic sealed orders seeking Ilvara’s whereabouts, unaware she had been consumed by Zuggtmoy’s influence and ceased responding.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing... Didn't you read the previous memo?

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove attempted political correspondence with Ilvara, but the communication failed because she had been pulled away by Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else.

subject: theological corruption of Ilvara
fact: Ilvara’s prayer book revealed a gradual theological corruption by Zuggtmoy, documented in marginalia that shifted from formal liturgy to associative, unstable writing.
source_quote: The early entries were neat and formal... then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in.

subject: discovery of Zuggtmoy-Lolth theological treatise
fact: A sealed wax pouch contained a meticulously written theological treatise arguing that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity, a conclusion reached through backward reasoning.
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration of why Zuggtmoy and Lolth — and claiming that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same thing.

subject: Drow Outpost
fact: The Drow Outpost was looted of personal, theological, and material artifacts that documented the descent of its occupants into Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: A cleric's catalogue of the things a high priestess of Lolth becomes when something older and stranger finds the seam in her theology and begins to work.

subject: wax pouch
fact: The wax pouch contained a theological treatise arguing the identity of Lolth and Zuggtmoy, written in close, careful script by a mind unraveling toward madness.
source_quote: Inside were pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book was a standard Lolth devotional text, but its margins contained a second, increasingly unstable handwriting that documented her subversion by Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: The Living Serpent Head Scourge was a weapon whose head was a sentient or partially animate serpent, preserved as a museum-grade artifact of terrible craftsmanship.
source_quote: It sounds like a great museum piece... You document them. You label them carefully. You do not pretend they aren't what they are.

subject: Drow cloak (spider-silk)
fact: A fine spider-silk Drow cloak, capable of drinking shadow, was taken from Asha Vandree’s body and claimed by Zalthir.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: flask of Overbright brandy
fact: A flask of Overbright brandy was received with personal interest, distinct from other looted items due to its intimate, sensory appeal.
source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

subject: water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: A water-damaged journal from an unnamed prisoner contained legible handwriting that showed the writer had kept records until they could no longer.
source_quote: The pages were swollen and the ink had run in places, but the handwriting was still visible in the drier sections.

subject: origin of Ilvara’s corruption
fact: The source of Ilvara’s subversion remains unknown — whether induced by another entity or self-initiated through altered consciousness — and the ambiguity is deeply troubling.
source_quote: I could not tell from the text whether she had known she wasn't resisting or whether she had genuinely believed she was still moving in her own direction.

subject: identity of the marginalia writer
fact: It is unclear whether the second handwriting in Ilvara’s prayer book was her own altered self or an external influence, leaving the nature of her corruption unresolved.
source_quote: Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: theological implications of Lolth-Zuggtmoy unity
fact: The treatise claiming Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity challenges the foundations of drow theology and may represent a new, dangerous heresy.
source_quote: It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during a looting operation at a Drow Outpost, following the deaths of Ilvara and Asha Vandree, and the discovery of their corrupted artifacts.
source_quote: Asha Vandree's body was next... The last item was on Ilvara herself.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend recovered a necromantic pearl from the heart of Ilvara's corrupted fungal ritual site and reclaimed his stolen tooth, marking the beginning and escalation of the corruption they faced.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket... I had the tooth back. And I had the pearl that had been buried in the heart of whatever she'd turned this place into.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan with no known noble lineage, yet he is the target of a high-value contract orchestrated by House T'sarran, suggesting his true value is hidden or misunderstood.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence... And yet, powerful Drow houses do not spend this kind of resource on nobodies.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, a High Priestess, used a fungal mass as a ritual anchor and wove Lolth’s web into Zuggtmoy’s sigil on a cloth artifact, revealing her dual allegiance and descent into madness.
source_quote: It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum destroyed the pulsing fungal growth clinging to the platform, using acid to purge Zuggtmoy’s corruption, demonstrating his intolerance for lingering evil.
source_quote: He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter... collapsed into ash in the time it takes to exhale.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran commissioned a contract to extract Daz alive and unharmed, using intermediaries and professional Drow mercenaries, indicating significant investment and hidden motives.
source_quote: There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym employed guards and a mage to escort the contract, all of whom perished in the chamber, suggesting the mission was compromised or intentionally sacrificed.
source_quote: The dead soldiers of House Mizzrym would never collect their pay.

subject: recovery of the necromantic pearl
fact: The necromantic pearl, a dense, hand-crafted object at the core of Ilvara’s fungal ritual site, was recovered and recognized as an unnatural artifact deliberately placed or grown under precise conditions.
source_quote: The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it.

subject: destruction of Ilvara's ritual cloth
fact: The ritual cloth, woven with Lolth’s web inside Zuggtmoy’s sigil, was recovered as evidence of Ilvara’s dual worship and psychological collapse, but not destroyed.
source_quote: It was evidence. It was Ilvara's madness made physical.

subject: purification attempt with Dawnbringer
fact: A proposal to use Dawnbringer in a ritual purification was rejected by the sentient sunblade, which insisted its purpose is to kill, not to sanctify.
source_quote: I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things.

subject: necromantic pearl
fact: A fist-sized, smooth, dense object of unnatural origin, found at the core of Ilvara’s fungal mass, radiating necromantic energy and resembling a worked stone rather than a natural growth.
source_quote: Smooth. Dense. Fist-sized. The weight of it was wrong for something grown — too even, too finished, like a stone that had been worked by a hand that knew what it was doing.

subject: ritual cloth
fact: A leather-wrapped artifact containing incense cones, a silver bowl, and a cloth stitched with Lolth’s web woven inside Zuggtmoy’s eight-fold sigil, symbolizing Ilvara’s fractured devotion.
source_quote: A cloth that had been stitched with two sigils — Lolth's web worked into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one woven inside the other.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: A sentient sunblade with strong opinions, refusing to be used as a ritual tool and insisting its function is exclusively combat-oriented.
source_quote: I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things. I will not be treated like a religious symbol...

subject: T'sarran signet ring
fact: A signet ring bearing the unmistakable seal of House T'sarran, found on the dead mage, confirming the house’s direct involvement in the contract to extract Daz.
source_quote: I found the signet ring first — House T'sarran, the seal unmistakable on the face of it.

subject: obsidian wand with captive spider
fact: An obsidian wand containing a preserved spider in amber, likely a focus for arcane or necromantic magic, recovered from the dead mage’s possessions.
source_quote: Then the wand: obsidian, a captive spider preserved in amber at its tip.

subject: Daz's true identity
fact: Daz’s mysterious value to House T'sarran, despite his apparent insignificance, creates an unresolved thread about his origins, potential hidden lineage, or undisclosed role.
source_quote: The gap between what I know about myself and what someone apparently believes about me was large enough to be, frankly, concerning.

subject: Ilvara's dual worship
fact: Ilvara’s fusion of Lolth and Zuggtmoy in ritual artifacts suggests a deeper, unexplained syncretic heresy that may extend beyond her personal madness.
source_quote: She'd been using as a ritual anchor... and the fungal growth... was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach.

subject: the purpose of the necromantic pearl
fact: The origin and function of the necromantic pearl — whether crafted or grown — remains unknown, but its placement at the core of a corrupted ritual site implies intentional design.
source_quote: A rock in the right place is a wall. The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident.

subject: after the fall of Velkynvelve
fact: The events described occurred after the party’s escape from Velkynvelve, marking the next phase of their journey and the unraveling of the conspiracy targeting Daz.
source_quote: When we'd first found ourselves hanging in nets at Velkynvelve...

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a sharp, expressive Drow sister who is deeply skeptical of Daz’s mysterious origins and dismissive of noble bloodline theories, yet professionally engaged in the investigation.
source_quote: That is an excellent question... Do you have daddy issues? Do you have mommy issues? Every drow thinks there's some noble things.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a calm, professional Drow sister who analyzes evidence with detached precision and offers brutally honest assessments, prioritizing duty over speculation.
source_quote: Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a pragmatic, analytical Drow who avoids emotional displays, treats mysteries as data to be audited, and seeks collective understanding over personal revelation.
source_quote: I think... we should investigate this together. Whatever we find... we split the proceeds.

subject: the fungal chamber
fact: A ruined chamber at the heart of Ilvara’s ritual site, filled with dead fungal matter, corrupted growths, and artifacts of her dual worship, now purged by Grygum’s acid.
source_quote: The fungal mass sat at the center of the chamber... Most of it was dead now. We'd done that.

subject: the surface road
fact: The path leading out of the underground ruins, now the next stage of the party’s journey, where unresolved questions about Daz’s identity and the necromantic pearl must be carried forward.
source_quote: Around me, the road to the surface waited.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir emerged into the Overbright after months of Underdark travel, having stopped trusting the surface world would be real, and now observes the group's reactions with quiet analysis, noting the transformation in others and himself.
source_quote: I stood and let the light happen to me. I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin led the group out of the tunnel, always instinctively at the front, and is now contemplating the history of Dawnbringer — a sword forged for radiance that endured prolonged darkness — and seeking a 'sword whisperer' to restore its connection to light.
source_quote: Thorin stood with his face at an angle that suggested he was calculating the sun's position relative to the year. He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum, the earnest half-orc, experienced a genuine spiritual moment in direct sunlight, opened the bag of holding, and is now focused on acquiring pamphlets and lore about Bahamut at Candlekeep, treating the Great Library as both research and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets. This was Grygum.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz emerged last, already observing and composing analysis before fully exiting, and is directing the group’s next steps toward Candlekeep to research House T'sarran, Jimjar’s disappearance, and his own hidden history — framing decisions as group discussions while subtly guiding them to his conclusions.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry. The decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz's call, framed as a group discussion but with Daz's particular analytical gravity already pulling it toward a conclusion before the conversation began.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz possesses the Stonespeaker Crystal, a key artifact from their Underdark journey, and is using it as part of his ongoing research into the group’s mysteries and his own past.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the gelatinous ward turned grey ooze and improbable companion, emerged from the bag of holding to experience sunlight for the first time, reacting with wide-eyed curiosity rather than fear — a response that contrasted with the group’s own awe and impressed Zalthir.
source_quote: Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze... had peered out. He had not been in sunlight before. He took it in the way a child takes in a first ocean.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth emerged with the rest of the surviving crew, but her specific actions and reactions are not detailed beyond her presence in the group's transition to the surface.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait emerged with the group, but no specific actions, dialogue, or reactions are described beyond being part of the surviving crew.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a target of research at Candlekeep due to its connection to Jimjar’s disappearance and the cryptic actions of hired Duskryns, suggesting a hidden influence on Daz’s past and the group’s current mission.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Duskryns
fact: The Duskryns are hired agents or operatives whose actions have pointed toward deeper secrets connected to Daz’s lineage and the group’s overarching mystery, prompting investigation at Candlekeep.
source_quote: whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep, the Great Library, is the chosen destination for the group’s next phase, serving as a hub for research into House T'sarran, Jimjar’s disappearance, Daz’s history, and Bahamut’s lore — a place of knowledge that aligns with both Daz’s analytical goals and Grygum’s spiritual ones.
source_quote: Candlekeep, the Great Library, research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance... Grygum was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage.

subject: The Overbright
fact: The Overbright is the surface world’s unfiltered sunlight — a phenomenon the group has not experienced in months, which transformed their perception of reality, triggered spiritual and analytical responses, and marked the end of their Underdark journey.
source_quote: The light that came through the tunnel mouth was not like Dawnbringer's light... It was a light that simply *was*, filling everything from every direction at once.

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: Blingdenstone is one of the Underdark locations the group traversed, surviving an ooze crisis and the bag of holding incident — now referenced as a milestone in Glabbagool’s survival and adaptation.
source_quote: Glabbagool had survived Blingdenstone, the ooze crisis, the bag of holding, and however many months of Underdark travel

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is Thorin’s ancestral sword, forged for radiance, which endured prolonged darkness in the Underdark and now requires restoration — its nature as a weapon of light is central to Thorin’s emotional journey.
source_quote: Dawnbringer... a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: The Stonespeaker Crystal is a magical artifact carried by Daz, used to record or interpret hidden truths, and is now central to his research into Daz’s own history and the group’s unresolved mysteries.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: Bag of Holding
fact: The Bag of Holding is a magical container used to store gear and companions — opened by Grygum, it released Glabbagool into sunlight for the first time, triggering a profound reaction.
source_quote: Grygum had opened the bag of holding... Glabbagool — our companion... had peered out.

subject: emergence into the Overbright
fact: The group’s emergence into the Overbright marked the end of their months-long Underdark journey, triggering physical, emotional, and spiritual transformations in every member, and initiating their transition to surface-world objectives.
source_quote: We stood in the Overbright for a while, longer than was probably necessary from a tactical standpoint, and nobody suggested moving immediately.

subject: Glabbagool's first exposure to sunlight
fact: Glabbagool’s first exposure to sunlight was a pivotal moment — his reaction of curiosity, not fear, redefined the group’s understanding of their companion and symbolized adaptation to a world they had long believed lost to them.
source_quote: He took it in the way a child takes in a first ocean, the way the sheer scale of a thing produces a silence that is not quite awe but is adjacent to it.

subject: decision to pursue gear over investment
fact: The group unanimously chose to spend their surplus gold on adventuring gear rather than business ventures, recognizing their survival depended on equipment, not infrastructure — a pragmatic decision reflecting their identity as survivors of the Underdark.
source_quote: We agreed on the gear.

subject: Daz's hidden history
fact: The origins and past of Daz remain obscured, with clues tied to House T'sarran, the Duskryns, and the Stonespeaker Crystal — a mystery driving the group’s research at Candlekeep and forming the core unresolved thread of their journey.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Jimjar's disappearance
fact: Jimjar vanished under mysterious circumstances linked to House T'sarran and the Duskryns — his fate is a key unknown the group seeks to unravel at Candlekeep, possibly tied to Daz’s own past.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: the sword whisperer
fact: The existence and location of a 'sword whisperer' — a specialist capable of restoring Dawnbringer’s connection to light — is an unconfirmed lead pursued by Thorin, forming a quiet but persistent thread of personal redemption.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about.

subject: months of Underdark travel
fact: The group spent an indeterminate number of months in the Underdark — a duration so prolonged it distorted their perception of time, memory, and reality, making the surface world feel alien and overwhelming.
source_quote: I genuinely cannot tell you how many months it had been. I had been thinking about this moment, intermittently, for months.

subject: weeks following emergence
fact: The weeks following the group’s emergence into the Overbright blurred into a period of recovery and adjustment, during which they slowly reoriented themselves to surface life, planned their next steps, and processed their transformation.
source_quote: The weeks that followed blurred in the way that recovery blurs — not forgetting, exactly, but the edges going soft.

subject: the monastery curriculum
fact: Zalthir recalls a forgotten lesson on material impermanence — possibly taught by Brother Quellin or a chalk-dusted instructor — that emphasized detachment from tools, a philosophical undercurrent that contrasts with the group’s reliance on gear and artifacts.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Some form of material impermanence — I think it was Brother Quellin... Something about a bowl and an empty hand.
